name: Central & Northern Ukraine (Kyiv · Polissia · Dnipro Basin)

language.script_notes: Ukrainian Cyrillic with і, ї, є and ґ; Russian is also widely spoken in Kyiv and the cities, though signage is in Ukrainian.

road_furniture.curb_style: Dense Soviet-era boulevard infrastructure in Kyiv.

architecture.roof_style: Golden and blue onion domes on Orthodox churches and monasteries; flat roofs on Soviet apartment blocks; pitched roofs on village houses.
architecture.roof_material: Metal and slate on houses; gilded copper on church domes.
architecture.wall_construction: Vast fields of khrushchyovka and later panel apartment blocks around Kyiv and every regional city; whitewashed clay mazanka houses with thatched or metal roofs in villages; grand Stalinist-era buildings along Kyiv's Khreshchatyk.
architecture.wall_color_palette: Whitewash with blue trim on village houses; grey and pastel panel blocks; gold and white on churches.
architecture.distinctive_building_types: Golden-domed Orthodox churches (Kyiv Pechersk Lavra, St Sophia); Stalinist and Soviet monuments; the abandoned buildings of the Chornobyl exclusion zone, which appear in Street View; whitewashed village houses.

nature.vegetation: Dense pine and mixed forest and marshland in the northern Polissia lowlands; black-earth farmland with sunflower, wheat and maize across the forest-steppe; willow and poplar lines along rivers and roads.
nature.terrain: Flat to gently rolling plains cut by the wide Dnipro River, with the Kyiv hills on its right bank and low, marshy forest to the north.
nature.climate_signature: Humid continental — green and forested in the north, opening into open, intensively farmed plains further south.

vehicles.distinctive_vehicles: A mix of older Lada and Soviet-era cars with used Western imports; marshrutka minibuses; trams and the Kyiv metro.

google_coverage.camera_generation: Mostly Gen 3 with a faint red hood sometimes visible.
google_coverage.coverage_notes: Good coverage in Kyiv and along main routes, mostly from around 2015; the Chornobyl exclusion zone has notable coverage of abandoned settlements.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Flat forested terrain, marshy Polissia landscape, Soviet panel blocks and Cyrillic signage
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Ukrainian letters (і, ї, є, ґ), flag-coloured painted roadside objects and blue-and-yellow plate strips separate Ukraine from Belarus.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Cyrillic script, black-and-white guardrails, Soviet architecture, similar farmland
confusion_set.tiebreaker: Ukrainian bollards are not attached to a narrow support pole (Russian ones are); the letters і, ї, є, ґ appear only in Ukrainian; white-painted pole bases are a Ukrainian tell.

confusion_set.shared_traits: Same country, same national road furniture
confusion_set.tiebreaker: The center and north is green forest-steppe and marsh with Kyiv's gilded domes; the west has Carpathian mountains and wooden churches, and the east and south is dry steppe.
